packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-14 - unverified blind image reading

Exposure: nothing in my context proposed an identification or reading of this text. I did nothing beyond the brief, except that I used `ls` on the packet directory to get the image filenames and `sips` to get the image pixel sizes.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-only)
- There are two faces of one narrow parchment strip, long and about 2 cm high in proportion. Face A is overview image-001 with tiles image-002 (left half) and image-003 (right half). Face B is overview image-004 with tiles image-005 (left) and image-006 (right). There is no scale bar.
- Face A:
  - Line 1, along the top edge: a darker, larger gothic textualis in brown-black ink. A red-touched capital stands mid-line, with a further red mark near the right end. The tops of the letters are trimmed by the cut edge.
  - Lines 2-3: a smaller, paler, more cursive hand, written lower on the strip with wide interlinear space. The ascenders and descenders are looped. Observation only: this could be a different hand or layer from line 1, for example a later addition or a gloss. That is tentative.
  - Further down the right end, faint traces of a 4th line and of a looped letter at the far right edge.
  - At the left end, a 2 cm band discoloured by adhesive. It has a slit, a turn-in or fold line, and no text.
- Face B: no text visible. It has stains, adhesive bands at both ends, a small red speck at the lower edge, and faint ruling? It is probably the blank or pasted side.
- Selected: all three lines on face A. Unread: the 4th-line traces (too faint).

TRANSCRIPTION
Line numbers count from the top of each tile. image-001 is the overview and duplicates both tiles.

== Face A, line 1 (larger script; image-002 continuing into image-003) ==
image-002 l.1  R(?) / ?Ry? ?Uenite? / ?Benite? / ?ue(n)ite?  ?benedicamus? / ?benedicentes? / ?bene dicamus?  ?d(omi)n(o)? / ?dnis?
image-003 l.1  [continues:] ?d(omi)n(o)? / ?-nus?  [red-touched initial: ?D? / ?N?]?ne? / ?ue? ?nobis? / ?uobis? / ?nr?  [red mark] ?T(?)? / ?F(?)? ?m? ?nn? [cut at right edge, letters truncated]
   Notes: the first group at the far left is small and has a cross-stroke. It may be a liturgical cue sign such as "R" or "Ant", or an abbreviated word ending "-enus"/"-enie". The second word is the clearest. I read it as "bene-" + "d?c" + "?mes/amus". The reading after the red initial is "?ue nobis?" / "?de nobis?". All low to medium confidence.

== Face A, line 2 (smaller cursive hand) ==
image-002 l.2  ?Undecim? / ?Vndetur? / ?Vadens?  ?qued? / ?quod? / ?pro?  ?d(?)? ?ude? / ?aude?
image-003 l.2  [overlap: "?ude?" again at left]  ?Ser? / ?Ego?  ?dumus? / ?domus? / ?dicere?  ?enim? ?ethe? / ?etiam?  [illegible]
   The row of ascenders above this line (image-002 at about y=300-380) belongs to this line's tall letters. They are not a separate line.

== Face A, line 3 (smaller cursive hand) ==
image-002 l.3  ?b(e)dsem? / ?Insur?  ?sp(iritu)s? / ?sapien(tia)? ?(?)? ?ner(?)? / ?ueniet?
image-003 l.3  [overlap at left] ?Se?/?le? ?quare? / ?quomodo?  ?in? / ?m?  ?nobis? / ?mortem?  ?A(?)?  ?fl(?)? [illegible, fades]

== Face A, traces ==
image-003, right end: faint letters below line 3 (?a 4th line?), plus a looped stroke at the cut edge (?"Se" / "d"?). [illegible]

== Face B (image-005, image-006) ==
No legible text. There may be faint ruling. I see possible faint ink offset around image-005 at about x=1500-1800 and image-006 at about x=900-1300, but no letter forms.

LIMITATIONS
- Line 1 is trimmed at the top, so ascenders and abbreviation marks may be lost. The red initial is partly faded.
- Lines 2-3 are in a pale, small, cursive hand on a stained ground, and nearly every word is uncertain. I offer alternatives and do not commit to one reading.
- I cannot tell from these images whether lines 2-3 belong to the same text as line 1 (e.g. continuing text) or are a later addition.
- Raking light or UV would help with lines 2-4. An image of the adjoining strip or of the binding position would show orientation and context.
